title: Second look at N-005: keep fragment 35 as a tentative internal image match
statement: I reviewed the Yale f89r2 fragment 35 crop and the f35v scan. Fragment 35 has a broad, rounded, lobed green crown; several short stalks converge at a thick brown spreading base, and its label sits beside the stalks. Folio f35v has a similarly broad lobed crown and a substantial brown root, so the proposed internal visual comparison is reasonable. The two drawings are not close copies: f35v also has a taller branching structure, winding branches, and separate berry-like clusters that are absent from fragment 35. Zandbergen’s 2012 slide describes f35v as tree-like, with oak suggested by the roots and crown, while noting that the fruit-like objects do not fit; it shows BnF Lat. 6823 f60r as a possible edera nigra comparator. Vatne also discusses f35v as resembling oak/ivy references, notes the missing ivy leaves, and considers an ivy-like root. These two discussions use the same BnF reference image, so they are not independent corroborations of an identification. I agree with N-005’s narrow conclusion: the crown/root resemblance supports a candidate internal image match, while the differing structures leave the plant identity and any name pairing unresolved.
sources: René Zandbergen, Voynich100 presentation (2012), pp. 24–25, including the f35v and BnF Lat. 6823 f60r comparison: https://voynich.nu/papers/Voynich100_RZ_2012.pdf
